explicit_non_claims: No production deployment, live cluster apply, or runtime rollout was executed from this branch.
No reviewer approval or remote protected-branch CI result is claimed before PR submission.
No direct core ownership of transient external policy or secret engines is claimed; owned adapter ports are the boundary.
No local command-oriented or text-interface product surface is introduced.

facets.F10_reversibility: All changes are code/config/evidence additions or edits on an isolated worktree branch and can be reverted through plain git; no live cluster or production data migration is performed.
facets.F11_observability: Typed usage events, circuit-breaker state, read-only MCP/status DTOs, OTel-minded worker ownership, and explicit Retry-After/failure states provide observable cloud surfaces.
facets.F13_migration: Converts reference behavior into Oyatie-owned cloud/Kubernetes resources and APIs while keeping external source data limited to provenance fields in the parity baseline.
facets.F1_correctness: Parity baseline contains 50 XPROXY rows, allowed statuses, target-test links, and source provenance; routing/pass-through, translation, pool, wire, tool compatibility, worker, and ops behavior is covered by focused tests.
facets.F2_tests: Focused Buck2 suites, full cloud-intelligence Buck2 test/build, rustfmt, YAML/JSON parsers, parity counts, naming-leakage scan, product-surface scan, transient-engine boundary scan, and diff-check are part of the local verification plan.
facets.F3_maintainability: New behavior is split across kernel, adapter, REST, translation, wire, tool-compat, workers, and ops crates with one-way dependency boundaries and typed DTO/resource models.
facets.F4_compatibility: OpenAI-compatible chat and embeddings routes preserve safe headers, strip hop-by-hop/provider-control headers, and expose compatibility/deprecation semantics for legacy request shapes.
facets.F5_security: Provider credentials are represented as owned secret-provider handles; request paths redact prompt/body/token material by default and do not add raw secret values or production credentials.
facets.F6_privacy: Usage/events/diagnostics avoid raw prompt, body, token, or secret logging; sticky routing uses privacy-preserving keys rather than raw prompt text.
facets.F7_operability: Kubernetes manifests declare gateway, controller/worker deployments, canary jobs, readiness/liveness, PDB, network policy, RBAC, and capability/config CRDs for cloud operation.
facets.F8_performance: Hot-path gateway logic remains separate from worker/controller reconciliation; pool headroom/stickiness/failover primitives model overload and Retry-After behavior without synchronous control-plane coupling.
facets.F9_compliance: Evidence records root-hub/docs/AGENTS review, parity status, no inherited internal identifier naming, and cloud-native-only implementation shape.

hyperscaler_lens.north_star: Productized cloud-intelligence operates as contract-first gateway/control-plane plus Kubernetes controllers/workers, not as a local operator workflow.
principles: owned abstractions for policy, secret provider, routing, and events
hot-path gateway separated from reconciliation workers
typed resources and tests before implementation behavior claims
source provenance retained without inheriting external identity into Oyatie identifiers
